title: Magic Knight Rayearth
subtitle: Three girls in Cephiro
summary: Magic Knight Rayearth is Sega's action role-playing game, first released for Saturn in Japan on 25 August 1995.
body: Magic Knight Rayearth is Sega's action role-playing game, first released for Saturn in Japan on 25 August 1995. Based on CLAMP's manga and its animated adaptation, it draws Hikaru, Umi and Fuu from a school visit to Tokyo Tower into Cephiro. They must become the Magic Knights and rescue Princess Emeraude to find a way home. The adventure follows that first major story while adding locations and characters of its own. Rieko Kodama directed a game that presents the three heroines as companions sharing a single journey through an unfamiliar world.

The party travels together, but only one heroine is active in a fight. The other two follow safely behind, and the player can switch the lead at any time. That arrangement turns the group into a tag team for enemies, puzzles and environmental dangers, making the choice of the active character part of handling the next obstacle. The inactive companions remain present without requiring the player to protect three separate figures simultaneously. Changing who leads therefore provides a direct way to use the party's variety within the same continuous adventure.

Each girl keeps a journal that gains entries after important events. Reading them gives the player another perspective on experiences already shared, allowing the companions' individual reactions to sit alongside the main story. Working Designs brought the game to North America in December 1998 after a lengthy localisation, making it that region's final Saturn release. The long delay placed an early Japanese Saturn adventure at the other end of the console's American life. Its illustrated presentation and three-character viewpoint preserved a very different kind of journey from the machine's prominent arcade conversions.
